# Successor candidate validation

The root [v0.8 candidate.5](../../../prodguild-openapi-v0.8-rest.json) is
**not frozen**. It is not generated by, or evidence of, the running backend.
All 60 original v0.7 operations/IDs remain; four recheck operations and employer
discovery are deferred. Candidate.5 records the spike's independent correction
review and **historical** held acceptance metadata. Its auth-only descriptions,
pending component signoffs and proposed integration shapes are retained historical
artifact content, not today's implementation status. The generator preserves those
facts; documentation relocation changes only its decision pointer.

The backend and active frontend now implement the learning, review, mentoring,
readiness and economy flows. See [architecture](../../../architecture.md#4-api-and-key-scenarios),
[product scope](../../../product.md#remaining-scope) and [runtime contracts](../../../src/backend/README.md).
Current routes/tests define behavior; existing implementations do not freeze this
candidate or make its differing schemas compatible. The following sections describe
candidate requirements and historical observations unless explicitly labelled runtime.

## Current runtime differences

- Durable SQL journals, request-scoped capture, exact queue-header replay, retained
  B/C and PR identities, historical grant snapshots, wallet mappings and the
  published-feedback worker exist. They are no longer unimplemented component gates.
- Runtime ASCII request keys are stricter than the candidate's length-only schema.
  File mutations return bounded metadata. Completion/quality/revision return
  ≤64KiB receipts; full draft responses allow at most20 comments and ≤512KiB capture.
  This differs from the candidate's200×10000 comment bounds and proposed read pages.
- Owner ledger history is sequence DESC. Runtime priority settlement/refund source
  fields reference ledger-entry UUIDs, not the historical proposed `pgw1` encoding.
- Files are bounded UTF-8 JSON only; binary/multipart materials/downloads are still
  unfinished. Native repo/PR links are null pending account/ACL provisioning.
  Published feedback uses general PR comments, not native inline review anchors.
- Current claim requires enabled review mode; the UI enables it before claiming.
  Assignments persist without deadlines; explicit owner return requeues and refunds
  a charged primary allocation once. Technical recovery leases remain separate.
  File-only draft comments with a path but no line are not accepted. Original API
  directory filters, custom file messages and several response/state shapes differ.
- Organizer drafts allow incomplete text/zero skills and optional client UUID
  creation deduplication. Catalogue q/difficulty/OR-skill filters run before pagination.
  Pinned-file comment ranges include unchanged lines; profile next_grade uses exact
  evidence. Migration `9337be067011` is required for these current contracts.

These differences remain visible without changing candidate routes, schemas or policy.

## Fresh owner-run corrections — bounded local observations

The owner-authorized disposable **SQLite** sandbox used official Gitea **28.1.0**:
`docker.gitea.com/gitea@sha256:f505a0d3a41323b786e05942fc7a4075e07ae7c169fd9485649aa55ee543a21a`.
The historical report's **66 rows remain disputed** because of scanner/classifier
correctness; its original artifact is unchanged. The final **sole-lead-owner**
correction run `prodguild-t01-lab-bf59da5559` passed **66/66 existing named matrix
rows**, recorded separately in [corrected evidence](evidence/local-matrix-correction.json).
This is actual bounded local evidence, not accepted full isolation. Independent
review covers corrections only; the reviewer did **not** operate the live lab.
The proposed topology remains a **private repository per project with a
same-repository PR**, separate private reference/draft-case repositories, and
protected retained B/C refs. The named observations cover mutation denial,
GC/restart survival and shared-upstream private-fork peer-diff leakage; shared
upstream PRs remain rejected.

Account-authorized read collaborators retain useful credential-free repo/PR links.
PR URLs may be null for unavailable resources or unprovisioned/unavailable account
ACLs. Separate Gitea login is required; app bearer tokens do not log into Gitea.
Historical browser/file/blob observations remain linked in
[local evidence](evidence/local-matrix.json), without changing that artifact here.
`local_read_write_matrix_complete=true`, `latest_fresh_complete=true` and
`new_live_proof=true` refer **only to the actual named corrected local observations**.
Both evidence metadata blocks identify the sole owner-run and the state
`owner-run-reviewed-corrections-local-bounded-observations`.
`latest_corrected_evidence_path` points to this correction artifact in both
contract-status and integration metadata; the historical path is kept separately.
Old test labels do not revalidate historical66/66; historical `local-matrix.json`
remains unmodified by this amendment.

The corrected evidence records policies
`prodguild-t01-actor-forbidden-body-canaries-v2` and
`prodguild-t01-gitea28.1.0-exact-native-denial-v1`: bounded actor-forbidden canary
inspection of the named responses/reachable fixture objects, and closed diagnostic
matching against the exact repository/protected ref with row-level denial reasons.
These are not universal encoding/surface proofs. Failed corrected attempts remain
separate: [01](evidence/local-matrix-correction-attempt-01.json) passed44/66 and
[02](evidence/local-matrix-correction-attempt-02.json) passed65/66; neither is erased
or relabelled by the final run.

Students can post **untrusted incidental comments**, but cannot edit/delete the
backend-authored canonical projection. Incidental annotations never determine
grades, grants, quality confirmation or rewards and do not require service-only
assessment repositories. PostgreSQL is authoritative, including review-comment
path/line/side/body metadata. Pending probation drafts/revisions and quality
feedback stay PostgreSQL-only; only published solution-review revisions are
projected after required confirmation. Restricted quality results never enter
learner-readable Git, including after solution-review publication.

Gitea compatibility observations require application/adapter safeguards:

- Concurrent lock-ref conflicts can return **403**; stale blob SHA can return
  **422**. Classify the operation and verified error semantics, translating these
  conflicts to business **409**. A blanket “every 403 is ACL denial” rule is wrong.
- Gitea accepted `new_position=999` with an empty hunk, unchanged README line 1,
  and both positions zero with an empty hunk. Application validation of the exact
  retained diff/path/side/line is mandatory. File comments keep the chosen general
  comment fallback with authoritative DB metadata; native acceptance proves no anchor.

## Historical acceptance and production proof limits

The recorded independent review was **corrections-only**, not full-matrix isolation.
Publication of corrected source `397ae3cfc8cbff20ef894257156e2b013d25839e` and bounded
fixture evidence did not freeze the contract. `isolation_proven=false` and held
component/full gates describe that candidate-era acceptance record, including the
then-held T02/T05 dependencies. Later application integration does not rewrite it.
`local_evidence` separates corrected owner-run observations from historical dispute
and from `approved_release`/`approved_image`. Local SQLite evidence cannot establish
production mirror approval, target PostgreSQL, VM/TLS/SSH or coordinated restore.

## Validation

From the repository root (tool dependencies are isolated; no application lockfile
or runtime dependencies change):

```sh
python3 tests/integration/gitea-spike/build_contract.py
uv run --no-project --with openapi-spec-validator==0.7.2 python -B tests/integration/gitea-spike/check_contract.py
uv run --no-project --with openapi-spec-validator==0.7.2 python -B -m unittest discover -s tests/integration/gitea-spike -p 'test_contract.py' -v
uv run --no-project --with ruff==0.12.12 ruff check --select E4,E7,E9,F,I --line-length 120 tests/integration/gitea-spike/build_contract.py tests/integration/gitea-spike/check_contract.py tests/integration/gitea-spike/test_contract.py
uv run --no-project --with ruff==0.12.12 ruff format --check --line-length 120 tests/integration/gitea-spike/build_contract.py tests/integration/gitea-spike/check_contract.py tests/integration/gitea-spike/test_contract.py
git diff --check
```

The validator checks OpenAPI 3.0 structure, every local reference, inline/schema/
media/header/parameter example, unique operation IDs, original operation retention
and phasing, GET safety declarations, request keys, creation Location, 204 bodies,
agreed numeric policy values, per-skill snapshots, explicit readiness and legacy
auth/health compatibility. All 60 original operations have audited, operation-specific
access rules retained in their descriptions: references are case-owner-only,
assignment/draft/workspace/source reads are assignment-scoped, catalogue/material
reads are published-only, and working files remain project-owner-only.
It also guards permanent project/submission business-key deduplication, active
priority/readiness deduplication and unchanged-existing200 semantics across
new/expired request keys, disputed historical/production evidence scope,
account-authorized PR links, canonical projection ownership, DB-only private
content and untrusted annotations. External refs/examples are forbidden. Example
semantic oracles test duplicate skill IDs, SQL-80/API-40 all-skill matching,
relevant expert confirmation and exact decimal XP. They are **not backend or
live ACL tests**.

The generator is reviewable amendment code over the preserved source. The offline
contract tests verify regeneration equality; CI currently does not run this suite.
Do not hand-edit the JSON and silently diverge.
Any future contract freeze must reconcile runtime shapes, status assertions,
release evidence, topology and contract version through explicit contract review.
There is deliberately no flag which turns this candidate into an accepted gate.

Key candidate decisions needing coordinator review:

- One project per participant/case and one submission per project, independently
  of request-key lifetime. An unchanged repeat returns the existing resource/PR
  and Location with 200; it creates no extra Git resource or job. Changed submitted
  content under a new/expired key conflicts; a retained key with changed payload
  still gives `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
- `difficulty` is derived from max case requirement (below 50 → `review_minus`,
  below 75 → `review_plus`, otherwise `expert`), not weight or authorization.
- Incomplete solution drafts are saved whole; final content is consumed by exact
  version. Final `approved` requires score ≥70; `changes_requested` requires <70.
- Quality assessment has its own score/decision/feedback and exact revision/claim,
  not an overloaded solution grade. Completed awaiting-quality/revision results
  do not occupy the one live assignment slot. Original reviewer revision rights
  never resurrect an expired/cancelled assignment; current skill grants still apply.
- Mandatory quality confirmation precedes author visibility and all effects.
- PR link nullability follows availability and account ACLs, not incidental
  annotation capability. No assumed SSO/SSH.
- Workspaces larger than the embedded snapshot bound return `snapshot=null` and
  immutable submission-scoped file/diff links, not an error or a HEAD fallback.
  `/submissions/{id}/files` and `/files/content?side=base|head&path=...` read the
  retained B/C tree. `/diff` and `/diff/lines` paginate changed files and pinned
  old/new coordinates, including deletions without native PR access. Both B/C
  refs are protected/retained. Diff text pages are bounded to 256 KiB, with explicit
  long-line text truncation and full bounded file reads available separately.
- An expert floor raised by the author's per-skill grade still requires independent
  confirmed expert rights; a provisional expert never satisfies any expert grade.
- Quality/revision/readiness creation Location identifies a retrievable singleton.
  Readiness application reads retain the expert's decision and actionable feedback.
- Bounds: text 1 MiB/file, binary 10 MiB/file, snapshot 200 files/2 MiB text.
  Query replacement path wins; any repeated multipart path must match exactly.
- Changed-key payload/in-progress/stale/capacity/funds errors are explicit409;
  oversized input413, invalid content422, hidden resources404, dependencies503.
  Empty allocation204 is cached: try again with a new request key.

These checks validate the candidate contract, not runtime business behavior or
live Gitea ACLs. They do not certify or block already-landed component integrations.

## Candidate.4/.5 authorization and retry decisions

### File and directory reads

All eight original content/directory GETs explicitly return422 for validation
errors. `FilePath` is required and nonempty; `DirectoryPath` omitted/empty selects
root. Nonempty directories share the same **1024 UTF-8 byte** bound, path checks,
object checks and one URL transport decode as files. JSON/multipart path values
and response paths are literal data, never percent-decoded. Reject absolute paths, empty/dot/
dot-dot components, backslash, NUL, case-insensitive `.git`, symlinks and submodules
at any traversed component. Never normalize away forbidden components or decode
again in the adapter. `%252e%252e/x` decodes to the **literal** `%2e%2e/x`, not
`../x`; storage must preserve that literal name. A directory on content GET or a
file on directory GET is422 `INVALID_PATH`; missing/hidden/foreign resources404.
Authorize before repository object lookup. Listings contain immediate children
and sort **path ASC, UTF-8 bytewise**, case-sensitive, without locale/directory-first
grouping, before pagination. The generic created-at ordering does not apply.

### Exact source revision, fail closed

`get_assigned_source_review` checks ownership and current all-skill confirmed
expert rights first: foreign/hidden/revoked access404. For the authorized owner:

| Condition | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `kind=review` | 409 `ASSIGNMENT_KIND_MISMATCH` |
| `kind=recheck` | 501 `FEATURE_DEFERRED` |
| expired/cancelled or lease elapsed | 409 `ASSIGNMENT_EXPIRED` |
| completed, with otherwise live lease | 409 `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE` |
| replaced claim, noncurrent revision, or nonpending review | 409 `STALE_REVISION` |
| live current quality claim, exact pending current revision | 200 |

On200, one consistent DB snapshot supplies
`assignment.revision_id == revision.id == review.current_revision.id` and the two
embedded revision objects must be identical, not merely share an ID. Submission
identity must also match the review. A denial contains only the safe error, with
no source content or current revision identifiers.
The validator pins **both404 and409** (including shared response references) to
the closed `Error` envelope. Substituting `AssignedReviewContent`, `ReviewResult`,
`ReviewRevision`, alternate media content or source-bearing `Error.details` fails
regression checks; matching descriptive prose alone is insufficient.

**Two-revision example:** expert E's claim pins R1. The reviewer subsequently
submits R2 and a new quality job is created. E cannot fetch R2 through the old
claim's nested `review.current_revision`: a still-assigned old claim gets409
`STALE_REVISION`; a completed old claim gets409 `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE` (or
`ASSIGNMENT_EXPIRED` if its lease has also elapsed). A foreign caller gets404
before those state checks. Direct pending review/revision reads also require a
live current exact-revision claim, otherwise404. A valid new claim on R2 exposes
R2 in both fields; no R1/R2 mixed payload is permitted. These are contract
oracles/regressions, not tests of the current runtime authorization implementation.

### Priority history and readiness authorization

- Priority singleton GET and owner list include **reserved, settled, cancelled
  and refunded** requests. Ownership is the read criterion; waiting-job/funds
  checks are purchase-only. Foreign singleton404; lists contain no foreign rows.
- Readiness applicant may self-read the application/assessments in every state
  without expert rights. Another reader or assessor must have **current confirmed
  expert rights in that exact skill** (`grade=expert`, `grant=confirmed`,
  `expert_confirmed=true`), independently of the applicant. No undefined assessor
  assignment is required: that qualification directly authorizes access.
  Applicant assessment POST403 `SELF_ASSESSMENT`; unrelated, supervised, revoked
  or role-only actors404. Assessment GET uses the identical read rule and verifies
  parent application identity. A past assessor snapshot does not override revoked
  current rights. Decisions lock/recheck pending status; terminal decisions409.

### Wallet ledger order — mapper proposal

`GET /api/v1/me/wallet/transactions` returns **only the current owner's** ledger,
all seven transaction kinds, ordered by **sequence DESC**. `WalletTransaction`
adds a required positive integer `sequence`, immutable and unique within that
owner's wallet; it is not a global sequence. Equal timestamps are allowed, and
neither timestamps nor UUID ordering controls ledger order. The existing
limit/offset parameters remain; new appended entries can shift offset pages.
The example includes welcome/rewards and reserve/settle/refund/release events
with equal timestamps to exercise sequence ordering. The candidate preserves its
historical mapper proposal; current owner ledger reads implement sequence ordering,
while other transport fields must be checked against the runtime guide above.

### Business deduplication beyond request-key retention

The generated `x-contract-scenarios` include new-key and expired-key examples:

| Existing business attempt | Equal facts | Changed facts | Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Priority `reserved` for owned primary job | 200 same request/reservation/Location | 409 `PRIORITY_ALREADY_ACTIVE` | no second hold/debit/request |
| Readiness `pending` for applicant/skill/grade | 200 same application/evidence/Location | 409 `APPLICATION_ALREADY_PENDING` | no second request or evidence replacement |

Priority facts are server-derived submission/job/cost/policy-version; POST accepts
no body or client-selected price/job. Readiness request facts are skill/grade;
new evidence accrued while pending leaves its original server snapshot intact.
The current request shape permits only grade `expert`: invalid grades/unknown
evidence fields still get422, not a replacement operation. A different skill is
a separate business key, not a mutation of the pending application. Active lookup
precedes first-purchase funds checks; depleted available funds after the original
reservation must not turn an equal repeat into an insufficient-funds failure.

Terminal history is permanent. Cancelled/refunded priority may have a **new**
attempt201 with new request/reservation/source IDs if the job is again waiting;
settled/assigned jobs cannot be purchased again. A terminal readiness application
may have a distinct new eligible attempt201 with fresh ID/evidence, subject to
current gates; an already-confirmed expert cannot reapply for the same grade.
Retained keys replay their bound original safe outcome rather than initiate new
attempts. Changed retained-key payload409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`; in-progress409
`OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`. Candidate examples are not DB tests; current persistence
and HTTP suites separately exercise concurrency, durable uniqueness and replay.

## Candidate-era integration recommendations

These historical proposals are not a current implementation inventory or a frozen
wire contract. Recovery/caching now exist with the runtime differences above.
The candidate `Idempotency-Key` schema remains length-only1..128. Its safe-ASCII proposal
`^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,128}$` is recorded in
`x-prodguild-integration-boundary.idempotency_key.proposed_for_t03_confirmation`,
alongside the then-pending T03 callback. Runtime adopted ASCII keys independently;
that does not retroactively change this candidate's schema or acceptance metadata.

1. **Cached queue header is an outcome snapshot.** Bind `X-Queue-State` to the
   original204 (`empty` or `no_eligible`), replay it unchanged with the same key,
   and do not consult the current queue or allocate on replay. A new key requests
   a new queue observation. Document this explicitly on the eventual header.
2. **Bind first201 and replay200 deliberately.** Persist the original outcome
   status, bounded safe body, canonical resource identity/Location and allowlisted
   headers together with the actor/method/path/key and canonical payload digest.
   The HTTP adapter sends first201 and successful-create replay200, preserving
   that resource/body/Location binding; it must not accidentally replay201 or
   create a new resource. DELETE/empty-queue204 remains204, bodyless. A safe
   original-state snapshot may differ from later GET history; it is never a fresh
   purchase or assessment. Generic journal “exact original status” semantics need
   this explicit endpoint replay-status mapping. New-key business dedup resolves
   the persisted active resource and binds its existing200 outcome separately.
3. **Bound upload digests and retain recoverable bytes.** Recommend a versioned
   canonical metadata envelope of at most4KiB for the single-file upload: method,
   canonical resource/effective decoded path, expected versions/blob, validated
   content metadata, actual byte count and lowercase SHA-256 digest. Compare
   repeated query/multipart paths before hashing; multipart boundary/order is not
   identity. Stream/hash with the existing1MiB text/10MiB binary limits, fail413
   on overflow, and avoid embedding/base64-copying content into the journal body.
   **A digest is not recovery data:** before external mutation persist an owned,
   access-controlled durable staging object plus its immutable recovery reference,
   byte count/digest and operation ownership. Verify staged bytes on recovery;
   retain them through terminal reconciliation/outbox needs and clean up with an
   explicit lifecycle. Crash after upload/intent/ambiguous Git success must recover
   the same content, not require a client reupload or invent bytes from a hash.
   The envelope bound and staging lifetime still need T03/T04 signoff.
4. **Replay reauthorizes before disclosing cached data.** Authenticate the current
   actor and recheck ownership/current grants, publication and exact revision
   access against authoritative state before returning any cached body, Location,
   PR link or download. Retained keys and historical assessor snapshots grant no
   access. Missing/revoked authentication401, hidden/foreign/revoked resource404,
   documented self-assessment403. Fail closed on newly private/stale content;
   never use old cached content as a fallback. Store only allowlisted bounded
   response fields/headers; exclude credentials, cookies, tokens, raw upstream
   errors and foreign/private projections. A pending source cache must satisfy
   the same current-claim/exact-revision checks as a fresh read.
5. **File mutation success is bounded metadata, not an echoed file.** Lead reports
   T03 follow-up `1055b0e` at branch tip `a71cc68` supports nested responses but has
   a hard1MiB **serialized response** ceiling. A permitted1MiB source text may
   exceed it after JSON escaping (for example1MiB of newlines needs over2MiB in
   JSON). Candidate text POST/PUT therefore returns existing `ProjectFile` with
   **`content=null`**; binary mutations retain `BinaryFileMetadata`. Fetch bytes
   through the authorized GET. Bound the **entire serialized success JSON
   envelope to64KiB UTF-8**, before finalizing a successful outcome; do not truncate
   metadata or report an uncached success. Source limits stay1MiB text/10MiB binary;
   this64KiB response cap is not a source-upload limit or a content-GET cap.
   First201/replay200 have the exact same metadata body and canonical Location;
   PUT200 replay also preserves the body, DELETE204 stays bodyless. Operation
   response schemas constrain text mutation `content` to null, and
   `x-prodguild-response-boundary` records the cap. Tests check the candidate
   shape and source-vs-serialized size distinction; the runtime text-only mapper
   now also uses bounded metadata, not the candidate binary implementation.
6. **Candidate binding mismatch: original review response capture does not fit T03.** The retained request
   schema allows200 comments of10000 characters. The reviewer's valid draft
   example serialized to2,010,953 bytes, above T03's hard1,048,576-byte ceiling.
   The regression constructs/validates another200-comment request and response
   and proves that even compact ASCII JSON exceeds2,000,000 bytes. Full
   `ReviewDraft`, `ReviewRevision`, `ReviewResult`, and their nested workspace,
   source, feedback and list representations can therefore exceed capture limits.
   `x-prodguild-integration-boundary.review_response_capture` declares
   **`compatible_with_t03=false`, `binding_gate=held`**; affected operations and
   schemas carry a held gate. These markers do not silently disable/accept new
   HTTP semantics: the candidate must not be bound as an accepted runtime API.

   Preferred design for coordinator/T03/T09 decision: return **metadata-only
   mutation outcomes ≤64KiB serialized JSON**, containing stable identity,
   exact version/revision, status, canonical Location and authorized content URI.
   Save full authoritative content and the bounded outcome atomically; return the
   same safe body on first response/replay with explicit201-to200 mapping. Retrieve
   content separately under current authorization, pinned to the exact saved
   version/revision. Propose **≤256KiB serialized JSON pages** for that read
   representation, including pagination of comments and other potentially large
   collections, with stable page/version coordinates and complete reconstruction.
   GET does not itself use mutation capture, but needs the coordinated content
   representation. These proposed shapes were not adopted into this candidate;
   existing review schemas/200×10000 bounds remain visible. Current runtime uses
   its own bounded receipt/draft contracts described above.
   No truncation, replay-only redaction, hash-only content recovery, fake
   collaborator or relaxation of T03's ceiling is permitted. The alternative of
   an aggregate input/output bound would require an explicit coordinated contract
   change, including escaping/Unicode accounting; it is not silently imposed here.

Lasting integration decisions now live in [architecture](../../../architecture.md#3-data-model):
retained B/C/PR identities, exact payloads, historical actor/skill evidence,
caller-owned transactions and wallet/source associations. Their adapters and
migrations exist; candidate metadata still records the original held mappings.
Corrected owner evidence and correction review remain bounded historical proof,
not successor-contract freeze or production acceptance.
